name: Bandipur
summary: A well-preserved Newari hilltop settlement between Kathmandu and Pokhara, sitting on a ridge above the Marsyangdi River valley. Known for intricately carved traditional architecture, cobblestone streets, and Himalayan views on clear days. Protected as a living heritage site. A convenient and increasingly popular stop for travelers moving between Kathmandu and Pokhara.

best_time_to_visit.primary: March to May (spring) and September to November (autumn)
best_time_to_visit.notes: Spring brings warm weather, rhododendron blooms, and lush green hiking trails. Autumn offers crisp air, sharp Himalayan views, golden rice-harvest terraces, and coincides with Dashain and Tihar festivals. Monsoon (June-August) brings heavy rain, humidity, and obscured views.

transport_options: Bus from Kathmandu to Dumre (5-6 hours) via Prithvi Highway, then local bus/jeep 8km uphill to Bandipur
Bus from Pokhara to Dumre (3-4 hours), then local transport to Bandipur
Private car/taxi directly from Kathmandu or Pokhara

difficulty_level: Easy (walkable town, optional moderate day-hikes nearby)
difficulty_notes: The town itself requires no trekking. Nearby optional hikes include Ramkot village (6km, ~1.5 hours one-way, easy) and Siddha Gufa cave (recommended with a guide, some sections require climbing with rope assistance).
things_to_do: Explore Newari architecture and cobblestone streets
Hike to Thani Mai temple for sunrise/sunset views
Visit Siddha Gufa cave (one of Nepal's largest caves)
Try Newari cuisine (samay baji, bara, choila) at local restaurants
practical_notes: No ATMs in Bandipur - bring cash from Kathmandu, Pokhara, or Dumre. Nearest medical facilities are in Dumre.
culture_notes: One of the few Newari towns outside Kathmandu Valley, founded in the 18th century by Newari merchants as a trade hub; wealthy merchant homes and temples reflect this history.
